# Lenz 0.0.18 beta

This release hardens how Lenz Diff and Lenz Code handle repositories, archives and project tools (PR #56). Updating is recommended for everyone on 0.0.17 or earlier.

- Lenz runs git with a stricter configuration. Mark resolved, Re-open and pull-request fetches no longer run git hooks; checkouts and branch creation still do.
- A pull-request fetch is refused when the repository's own config sets network or credential keys. The same keys in your global git config still work.
- Partial clones are never fetched from while Lenz reads them. On git older than 2.45, partial-clone repositories are refused.
- Archive members compare by content (SHA-256) instead of size and CRC. Archives with repeated paths, PAX sparse members or encrypted zip members are no longer shown as folders.
- Folder comparison follows only your own git excludes: files hidden by `.git/info/exclude` or a repository's `core.excludesFile` are now listed.
- Lenz Code runs a project's own `tsc`, virtual-environment Python, `ruff` and `black` only after **Trust Project Tools in This Folder**, in both the desktop and terminal command menus. **Stop Trusting Project Tools in This Folder** reverses it.
- Lenz Code's settings, recent folders and project state are now readable only by you. The trash refuses trash folders owned or writable by other users.
- SVG files get a Source mode that compares the text next to the rendered view. Files whose encoding can hide ASCII text show a notice.

## Costs

Comparing archives is slower, because every member is now read: 5000 small zip members take 47 ms instead of 3 ms, and 32 members of 2 MiB take 113 ms instead of 3 ms. The PostgreSQL syntax check in Lenz Code takes about 30 µs instead of 1 µs.

## Validation

The release commit passes the full local Linux gate and `scripts/perf-check.sh`. Native macOS interaction, the fish shell, git versions older than 2.56 and GitHub Enterprise hosts remain unverified. Native package build/signature and CLI checks are separate from interactive validation. macOS packages are ad-hoc signed.

Keep all five executables together. Verify the matching `.sha256` sidecar before installation.

[Changes since 0.0.17](https://github.com/aantoniadis/lenz/compare/v0.0.17...v0.0.18).
